RECOMMENDATION: IT DEPENDS
LIKELIHOOD: 60

An all-male panel selecting a candidate with roughly half your experience using subjective criteria ("client relationships"), combined with unexplained silence, presents recognizable indicators of implicit or affinity bias. However, leadership selections also heavily weigh business development, commercial networks, and interview dynamics. 

Directly raising the panel’s gender right now may prompt defensiveness and close doors before you receive useful information. Instead, send a professional follow-up requesting your detailed competency scoring and feedback. If the firm remains evasive or cannot provide objective criteria justifying the decision, you will have stronger grounds to raise procedural fairness and panel composition through HR, an employment specialist, or a formal grievance.
